RQ1: What is the impact of model architecture and training environment on image classification training concerning energy consumption and GPU usage?

Santiago del Rey

Load data

We load the data from the parquet file. We filter out the inception_v3 architecture and the Local Normal User training environment, as they are not relevant for RQ1. We also normalize the energy consumption by the total number of images seen during training and convert the energy from MJ to J for analysis.

df <- read_parquet("../data/metrics/processed/dl-training-energy-consumption-dataset.gzip") %>%
  filter(architecture != "inception_v3" & `training environment` != "Desktop Normal User" & `return code` == 0) %>%
  mutate(
    energy = (`energy (MJ)` * 1000000) / `total seen images`, # Convert MJ to J and normalize by total seen images
    training_environment = factor(`training environment`),
    architecture = factor(architecture),
    gpu_usage = `gpu usage (%)`,
  )

clean_data <- df %>%
  group_by(architecture, training_environment) %>%
  mutate(
    Q1 = quantile(gpu_usage, 0.25),
    Q3 = quantile(gpu_usage, 0.75),
    IQR = Q3 - Q1,
    is_outlier = gpu_usage < (Q1 - 1.5 * IQR) | gpu_usage > (Q3 + 1.5 * IQR)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

filtered_data <- clean_data %>%
  filter(!is_outlier) %>%
  dplyr::select(-Q1, -Q3, -IQR, -is_outlier)
head(df)

Data summary

filtered_data %>%
  group_by(architecture, training_environment) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_gpu_usage = mean(gpu_usage, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_gpu_usage = sd(gpu_usage, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_gpu_usage = min(gpu_usage, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_gpu_usage = max(gpu_usage, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = n()
  )
`summarise()` has grouped output by 'architecture'. You can override using the
`.groups` argument.
hist(filtered_data$gpu_usage, breaks = 30, main = "Distribution of GPU usage")

boxcox(lm(gpu_usage ~ architecture * training_environment, data = filtered_data))

Create a linear mixed model

We create a linear mixed model with gpu_usage as the response variable and training_environment and architecture as fixed effects. We also include an error term for the subject variable to account for the fact that it is a random effect.

filtered_data$gpu_usage_sq <- filtered_data$gpu_usage^2
model <- lm(gpu_usage_sq ~ architecture * training_environment, data = filtered_data)

summary(model)

Model diagnostics

We check the model diagnostics to ensure that the LMM is appropriate for the data.

sim_res <- simulateResiduals(fittedModel = model)

testDispersion(sim_res)        # Should not be significant


    DHARMa nonparametric dispersion test via sd of residuals fitted vs.
    simulated

Significance testing

# For linear models
options(contrasts = c("contr.sum", "contr.poly"))  # sum-to-zero contrasts for Type III
Anova(model, type = 3)

Post hoc tests

emm <- emmeans(model, ~ architecture * training_environment)
